mobility aid = a device such as a stick, frame or wheelchair that helps a person move
guide dog = a trained dog that helps a blind or visually impaired person travel safely
Braille = a system of raised dots that blind people read by touch
carer = a person who looks after someone ill, elderly or disabled, often unpaid
long-term care = ongoing help with daily life for people who cannot live fully independently
step-free access = a route into a building or vehicle that does not require climbing steps
first aid = simple medical help given before professional care arrives
recovery position = lying someone on their side so the airway stays open if they are unconscious but breathing
CPR = chest compressions, and sometimes rescue breaths, to keep blood moving when the heart has stopped
defibrillator = a device that can restart the heart with a controlled electric shock
abdominal thrusts = inward and upward presses on the upper abdomen to clear a blocked airway
triage = sorting patients so the most urgent cases are treated first
medical emergency = a sudden, serious health event that needs immediate professional help
emergency services = organisations such as ambulance, fire and police that respond to urgent incidents
adrenaline auto-injector = a device a person at risk of anaphylaxis can use to inject adrenaline quickly
blood donation = giving your blood so it can be used for patients who need it
donor card = a document showing you agree that your organs may be used after death
euthanasia = intentionally ending a person’s life to relieve suffering from a terminal illness, illegal in many countries
medical certificate = an official note from a doctor confirming illness or fitness
vital signs = basic measurements such as pulse, temperature, breathing rate and blood pressure
